evidence_summary: Maestro was the CMI/Gibson-associated effects brand. The FZ-1 was introduced in 1962. This entry treats Maestro/CMI as the manufacturing organization while preserving later factory changes by model revision.
Model-level production evidence places FZ-1A manufacturing first in Kalamazoo and later in Lincolnwood, Illinois. This is a manufacturer/product census entry, not a single-factory claim.
FZ-1B is a distinct later Maestro product, with period production attributed to Lincolnwood, Illinois. The model is cataloged separately from the earlier germanium FZ-1/FZ-1A family.
Maestro historical material identifies FZ-1S as a later 1970s fuzz product. Model-level factory documentation is thinner than for the earlier FZ-1 series, so it remains research-only.

Baldwin-Burns is a distinct manufacturer/brand organization associated with the Buzzaround. The Buzzaround appeared on a Burns price list in 1966 and was produced in meaningful quantities into the late 1960s. The builder is kept separate from Sola Sound despite circuit-family comparisons.

Selmer developed its own Buzz Tone by August 1966. Fuzzboxes notes Selmer equipment was manufactured at a Holborn, London factory during the period, making Selmer the current best builder attribution for the model.

The Buzz Tone circuit was later redesigned into Selmer's more sophisticated Fuzz-Wah, introduced in 1968. The product belongs in the builder census, while exact factory documentation remains thinner than for the Buzz Tone.

Arbiter had its own factory at 33 Woodthorpe Road, Ashford, Middlesex, and developed the Fuzz Face in 1966. Production continued through the Dallas-Arbiter period before later ownership/manufacturing changes.

Vintage Guitar reports that John Hornby Skewes commissioned Wilsic Electronics in Doncaster to design and build his early stompboxes. Charlie Ramskir and Wilsic are therefore recorded as the physical builder for the Zonk Machine marketed by Hornby Skewes.

Specialist historical sources identify a less-expensive silicon Zonk II associated with Wilsic Electronics. The product is retained as research-only until a stronger period model-level source is located.
